final_answer.summary: Heuristic lung-actionability triage for the five-gene panel: EGFR, ALK, MET, and ERBB2 are directly targetable in NSCLC with FDA-approved therapies; PIK3CA is exploratory only and was deprioritized because I found no lung-specific FDA-approved targeted therapy.

ranked_targets.evidence_basis: Multiple FDA-approved NSCLC indications; strongest broad panel utility.
FDA-approved for both adjuvant and metastatic ALK-positive NSCLC.
FDA-approved for metastatic NSCLC with MET exon 14 skipping.

approved_lung_filters: HER2 (ERBB2) tyrosine kinase domain activating mutations
ranked_targets.evidence_basis: FDA accelerated approval in 2025 for non-squamous NSCLC with HER2 TKD activating mutations.
Lung relevance exists, but I found no lung-specific FDA-approved targeted therapy; treat as pathway-exploratory rather than ranked therapeutic target.

shortlist.rank_reason: Broadest and most established EGFR-mutant NSCLC coverage.
Standard ALK-positive NSCLC option with adjuvant and metastatic labeling.
Direct MET exon 14 skipping target with regular FDA approval.
Latest HER2-mutant NSCLC option identified in public FDA evidence.
Prior approved HER2-mutant NSCLC option; fallback if an ADC is preferred.

notes: EGFR is only actionable here for exon 19 deletion or exon 21 L858R disease.
ALK is actionable only for ALK-positive / rearranged tumors.
MET is actionable only for MET exon 14 skipping alterations.
ERBB2 is actionable only for HER2 (ERBB2) activating mutations, especially TKD activating mutations.
